THIS IS AN ADDITIONAL UNIT. The repository already has a unit, and agents have taken the easy gains there: most recent attempts found nothing more to improve. Existing units, with what was achieved on each target:
- unit base58-rs (0 accepted generations); a patch may change: src/**; tests: `cargo test --release --locked --offline --no-fail-fast 2>&1`
  - encode_ir (perf): `valgrind --tool=cachegrind --cache-sim=no --cachegrind-out-file=/dev/null target/release/examples/lineage_bench encode "$LINEAGE_SEED"`; calibrated 250433520; no accepted change yet
  - decode_ir (perf): `valgrind --tool=cachegrind --cache-sim=no --cachegrind-out-file=/dev/null target/release/examples/lineage_bench decode "$LINEAGE_SEED"`; calibrated 93421131; no accepted change yet
  recent work: of its last 9 final attempts 9 ended without an improvement and 0 were accepted

Your unit must add headroom those units do not have. Choose one or more, by reading the code:
(a) another part of the code: a module, package or crate the existing units do not let a patch change, which has tests of its own; allow only that part;
(b) a heavier or more realistic workload on the same code, as NEW targets with their own names (for example encode_long_ir, decode_batch_ir): larger and more varied inputs, the calls real users make, so that the library's own work is nearly all of each count;
(c) more targets: operations of the library that no existing target measures, and binary size where this class measures it.
Keep the prepare, build and test commands of the format reference (it is this repository's own unit) unless the new part of the code needs others.

Two rules are checked for an additional unit:
1. No duplicate. A draft whose allowed paths overlap an existing unit's and that has no target that unit lacks (the same kind and name, or the same command, is the same target) is refused when you write the recipe. Name every new target for what it measures.
2. Headroom. Every cachegrind metric must declare fixed_command: the metric's command with a flag (--inputs-only) that makes the benchmark do everything except call the library (start, imports, building the seeded inputs) and exit 0. The trial measures it, and fails unless it is at most 10% of the metric. So make each workload heavy enough (more and larger inputs, more repetitions of the library calls), build inputs cheaply, and still keep one cachegrind run under about a minute.
In recipe.yml a metric then reads:
  - name: encode_long_ir
    ...
    command: <the cachegrind command> encode_long $LINEAGE_SEED
    fixed_command: <the same command> --inputs-only
If the repository has nothing more to measure (one small module, already covered), call give_up with impossible true and say so.

proposal.name: base58
proposal.note: Additional unit for debris/base58 with two new workloads on the single codec module, which the existing unit does not measure. encode_long_ir encodes 300 to 2048-byte blobs, where the quadratic byte-at-a-time encoder (one divide by 58 per inner step) is nearly all of the count, so limb-wise or batched conversion has large headroom. decode_short_ir runs 80k decodes of short strings (6 to 44 digits, some with leading '1's). The decoder always walks its full 33-limb accumulator for every digit and makes a copy on each call, so per-call and per-digit overhead dominates. Inputs are built without calling the library. The fixed part is 0.2% and 3.8% of the two counts. The equivalence harness adds long encodes and many short decodes to the earlier edge cases. Upstream tests also run from a protected verbatim copy.
